title: Lipschitz Dueling Bandits over Continuous Action Spaces
claim: The algorithm's reference arm converges quickly to the optimum and yields substantially lower regret than a naive discretization baseline.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, contour map, convergence curve, regret curves
description: A row of three plots with captions below. (a) A 2D filled contour map on the unit square, from purple (low) to yellow (high), with a colorbar. A red star marks the optimal arm near (0.3, 0.1), black crosses mark final arms from 50 runs clustered tightly around it, and a blue dot marks the initial arm at the upper right. (b) A blue line with a shaded confidence band shows the gap between the reference arm and the optimum falling steeply over 7 rounds, then flattening near zero. (c) Regret against time horizon for two methods. The orange uniform-discretization line grows nearly linearly to about 4, while the blue ARC-DUELLI curve is clearly lower and sublinear, ending near 2.
caption: Recursive cube exploration (RoundFunc)
abstract: We study for the first time, stochastic dueling bandits over continuous action spaces with Lipschitz structure, where feedback is purely comparative. While dueling bandits and Lipschitz bandits have been studied separately, their combination has remained unexplored. We propose the first algorithm for Lipschitz dueling bandits, using round-based exploration and recursive region elimination guided by an adaptive reference arm. We develop new analytical tools for relative feedback and prove a regret bound of $\tilde O\left(T^{\frac{d_z+1}{d_z+2}}\right)$, where $d_z$ is the zooming dimension of the near-optimal region. Further, our algorithm takes only logarithmic space in terms of the total time horizon, best achievable by any bandit algorithm over a continuous action space.
